ambiguities.description: The mentoring fact type is described as acyclic ('cannot have loops... not even indirectly through a chain') as well as irreflexive and asymmetric. It's unclear if 'acyclic' subsumes asymmetric/irreflexive or if all three should be modeled distinctly; also unclear if intransitive applies (mentoring likely not transitive, but this is not explicitly stated beyond loop prevention).

source_references.excerpt: No, never. And you cannot have loops either -- if Alice mentors Bob, then Bob cannot mentor Alice, not even indirectly through a chain. Mentoring always flows one way.
